source: Arduino Nano (A000005) datasheet / Eagle files: PCB 45 x 18 mm (the task sheet's figure, which includes the mini-USB overhang; the bare Eagle outline is 43.2 x 17.8 mm), four mounting holes about 1.7 mm (the official drawing shows 1.8 mm on a 43.2 x 15.2 mm pattern, 0.9 mm from the short edges and 1.4 mm from the long edges), two 15-pin rows at 2.54 mm pitch, rows 15.24 mm apart, mini-USB B receptacle on a short edge. ASSUMED / uncertain: PCB thickness 1.6 mm (+/-0.1), mini-USB receptacle 7.7 x 9.0 x 3.9 mm overhanging the edge by 0.7 mm (+/-0.5, clone boards differ), tallest top part 3.5 mm (reset tact switch; ATmega TQFP is 1.4), header plastic 2.5 mm on the underside with 6 mm pin tails (the header is soldered on the bottom). Check against the owner's board and the official drawing.
frame: module: origin at the PCB min corner, PCB bottom at Z = 0, components on +Z, mini-USB end at -X, header body on the underside (-Z)

pcb_length.source: task sheet: board outline along the header rows (official bare PCB 43.2)

hole_diameter.source: task sheet: mounting holes about 1.7 mm (official drawing 1.8)

hole_from_short_edge.source: official drawing: pattern 43.18 mm on a 45 mm outline -> 0.91 mm

hole_from_long_edge.source: official drawing: pattern 15.24 mm on an 18 mm outline -> 1.38 mm

usb_width.source: mini-USB B receptacle body width (typical SMD shell)

usb_depth.source: mini-USB B receptacle body depth (typical SMD shell, assumed)

usb_overhang.source: assumed receptacle overhang beyond the PCB edge

header_body_height.source: standard 2.54 mm header plastic height, on the underside

pin_tail_length.source: assumed pin length below the plastic (Nano ships with the long pins down)

top_parts_height.source: assumed tallest top-side part (reset tact switch)

interfaces.source: catalogue data (generalize iteration 001, delta D1): the mounting-hole axis list, the plane the part rests on when seated over its holes, and the plane its component keep-out starts from

notes: Mounting holes: the 0.9 mm edge distance leaves almost no land beside the hole, so a standoff boss of the HOLE keepout_diameter (4.0, assumed: M1.6 screw head or 1.7 mm pin tip) overlaps the PCB edge by design; use pins/posts through the holes or edge ribs if a boss cannot be placed. The header body is on the underside, so the board must stand on its HOLE posts or on the long-edge strips clear of the pin tails (pin_tails_a/b keepouts, which model pins pointing down to be plugged into a breadboard; shorten pin_tail_length if the owner's pins are cut). The ATmega328 and USB-serial chip (<= 1.4 mm) lie inside component_side. Import gate: R1 matches the PCB; R2 hole diameter/pitch from the official drawing +/-0.2; R3 USB along -X; R4 receptacle overhang is an assumed value (tol 0.5); R9 is skipped (no STEP imported).
